source_locator.passage_anchor: IN Questions concerning sick People
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: In questions about sick persons, use the ascendant, its ruler, and the ruler of the figure as significators for the sick person.
prerequisites: Horary question concerning a sick person.
exceptions_and_modifiers: These are roles in a historical horary method, not three independent observations.
The source does not define the ruler of the figure as automatically identical to the ascendant ruler.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: From the Signe of the sixt
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Judge the alleged illness and affected part using the sixth-house sign and ruler, planets placed there, and the lunar position and sign, all in relation to the ascendant.
prerequisites: Illness or affected body part is asked about.
Sixth sign, ruler, occupants, and lunar place are inspected together.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Do not reduce the multiple specified inputs to the sixth cusp alone.
An illness/body-part mapping here is premodern doctrine, not a medical diagnosis.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The seventh house represents the Physician
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The seventh house signifies the physician and the tenth his medicine; an unfortunate ruler of the seventh is said to prevent the physician curing, while misfortune of the tenth or its ruler indicates improper physic.
prerequisites: Medical horary figure.
Assess separately the seventh-ruler state and tenth-house/tenth-ruler state.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Provider, medicine and patient significators are distinct.
Failure and treatment appropriateness are claims of the historical text, not evidence.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The fourth house signifies the end of the sicknesse
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The fourth house indicates the disease's ending: fixed signs imply prolongation, common signs variation, and movable signs an ending or change relatively quickly.
prerequisites: Judge end or duration of sickness.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The source says the movable ending may occur one way or another, not invariably recovery.
Do not convert sign classes to exact calendar duration.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: That Physician who first visits
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A physician first visiting in Saturn's planetary hour is said to face prolonged sickness or treatment and torment, with cure only near the time both physician and patient almost despair.
prerequisites: Planetary hour at FIRST physician visit is Saturn's.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The text offers long illness OR long cure, not both necessarily.
No verified physician-patient outcomes or causal evidence.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: He that first enters upon a cure
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Beginning a cure in Mars's planetary hour is said to produce a patient disaffected toward the practitioner, dismissive of medicine and paying or respecting the practitioner poorly.
prerequisites: Planetary hour when physician FIRST begins cure is Mars's.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Beginning treatment is different from the first visit of #5/#7.
Patient conduct predictions are unsupported historical descriptions.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: He that first visits his Patient
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: At a first visit in Jupiter's or Venus's hour, the source expects good words, esteem and payment, and says even a failed cure should not harm the physician's reputation.
prerequisites: Planetary hour at FIRST physician visit is Jupiter's OR Venus's.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The final author gloss limits no prejudice specifically to reputation or estimation, not efficacy.
Reputation/payment are not evidence of cure.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: When a Urine is brought
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: When the patient's urine is brought, assign the ascendant to the sick person regardless of whether the querent has that person's consent; the source invokes urine as sometimes part of the sick person's essence.
prerequisites: A urine specimen has been brought to the physician.
exceptions_and_modifiers: No medical diagnostic validity of urine-as-essence is established.
This is the local exception to questioner-signification, not permission to ignore consent in real care.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If no Urine or consent of the sick party
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Without urine or the sick person's consent, the source assigns the ascendant to the questioner; locate the patient and illness by the questioner's relationship. In a master's servant enquiry, the sixth signifies servant and sixth from that sixth (the eleventh) is used for disease.
prerequisites: The original prints no urine OR consent, a grammatically ambiguous combination; preserve the 'or' rather than silently requiring both absent.
The questioner is distinct from the patient.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Keep derived sixth-from-sixth = eleventh and relation-specific house assignment.
This item begins on PDF316 and continues on PDF317.
Do not treat historical lack-of-consent procedure as an acceptable modern medical practice.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: But in every Disease have care
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: In every illness question, the Moon's position is to be considered as a general significatrix.
prerequisites: Any illness question.
exceptions_and_modifiers: General significance does not replace the local conditions and house significators.
Aphorism not an independent empirical outcome.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The sick party is in great danger of death
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The source says great danger of death when BOTH Sun and Moon are below the Earth at the time of questioning OR first invasion of sickness.
prerequisites: At question time OR first onset (choose the relevant context).
Both luminaries must be below Earth.
exceptions_and_modifiers: This is a dangerous prognostic claim in a historical source, not a reliable clinical assessment.
No substitute of one subterranean luminary for both.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: As no light is in this World
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: No hope of recovery is asserted when the luminaries are obscured or subterranean at the first lying down, with a stronger alleged death testimony if either is afflicted.
prerequisites: At initial decumbiture.
Both lights obscured or below Earth as the source states.
At least one afflicted luminary for the intensified death testimony.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Distinguish base condition from subsequent aggravating condition.
Overlaps item11 and must not count as a statistically independent vote.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The square or Opposition of the Fortunes
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Squares or oppositions of the benefics are said not necessarily to destroy, nor do favourable aspects of malefics profit unless reception accompanies the aspect.
prerequisites: Square/opposition of one or more fortunes OR a favourable aspect from an infortune.
Reception is specified to permit a malefic's favourable aspect to benefit.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Asymmetric claims: negative benefic aspect not necessarily destructive, positive malefic aspect not necessarily helpful.
No generic unconditional benefic/malefic scoring.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Sun and Moon, or Lord of the Figure
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Freedom from affliction and lack of connection to the eighth-house ruler among the luminaries, figure ruler or ascendant ruler are said to indicate recovery; if two such significators are so affected, the patient fares well; otherwise death is asserted.
prerequisites: Consider Sun, Moon, lord of figure, lord of ascendant.
Favourable condition combines no affliction AND no affinity with eighth ruler.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Original 'or' between significators and 'two of these Significators be so affected' have scope ambiguity; preserve instead of imposing a precise count rule.
The otherwise-death claim is source rhetoric, not calibrated or clinical.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Lord of the ascendant in his Falls
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A fallen, unfortunate or combust ascendant ruler, or the figure ruler in the condition described, yields the printed ambiguous warning that it is 'doubtfull' the person 'will dye' of the infirmity.
prerequisites: Ascendant ruler in its fall, unfortunate, OR combust; alternatively examine the figure ruler as printed.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Preserve 'doubtfull' rather than turning the statement into a certain death prognosis.
Pronoun/syntactic scope for figure ruler remains uncertain.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: When the Significator of the sick is feeble
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A feeble sick-person significator and a strong eighth-house ruler afflicting it are said to create fear of death during the current illness.
prerequisites: Sick-person significator weak.
Eighth-house ruler strong AND afflicting that significator.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Author adds a nature-weak/disease-prevalent rationale, not a separately measured mechanism.
Risk asserted, not certain death.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Lord of the ascendant be placed in the eighth
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: If the ascendant ruler lies in the eighth and is received by its ruler in an essential dignity, the sick person is said to recover beyond expectation, even without reciprocal reception.
prerequisites: Ascendant ruler in eighth.
Eighth ruler receives ascendant ruler by some essential dignity.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Source explicitly allows the ascendant ruler not to receive the eighth ruler back.
Reception is not synonymous with conjunction or mere co-presence.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Physician may justly feare his Patient
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Fear is prescribed when both the ascendant ruler and Moon apply by adverse aspect to a planet below the Earth; the contrary is expected if the applications are to a planet above Earth.
prerequisites: Ascendant ruler AND Moon applying by ill aspect.
Their target planet below vs above Earth determines source contrast.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Printed above-Earth house list is twelfth, eleventh, ninth, eighth and seventh; the tenth is not explicitly in the list, so do not silently complete it.
The remainder is called below-Earth in the passage; house geometry is source-specific.
No patient care guidance.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Lord of the eighth being on the cusp
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: An eighth-house ruler on the cusp of the tenth combined with an ascendant ruler below Earth leads to the literal source warning 'great fear of recovery'.
prerequisites: Eighth-house ruler at tenth cusp.
Ascendant ruler below Earth.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The printed polarity 'fear of recovery' appears odd relative to neighbours; retain exactly, do not silently change to fear of death or no recovery.
Requires source comparison before executable Boolean interpretation.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Moone be swift in course
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A swift and waxing Moon applying by sextile or trine to the ascendant ruler is said to hasten cure; reception makes cure easier, and application above Earth is said to be sooner still.
prerequisites: Moon swift AND increasing in light.
Moon applies by sextile OR trine to ascendant ruler.
Reception, when present, is an additional modifier.
Target above/below Earth modifies judgment.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Source expressly permits favourable application even below Earth; do not require above-Earth in the base rule.
No exact day or duration conversion.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Lord of the ascendant be in the sixt
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Ascendant ruler in the sixth OR sixth ruler in ascendant is said to prolong illness and signal affliction; square/opposition of the two rulers likewise is adverse.
prerequisites: Ascendant ruler in sixth OR sixth ruler in ascendant; alternatively square/opposition of sixth ruler to ascendant ruler.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Multiple alternative triggers rather than a conjunction of all.
Does not by itself assert death.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the two benevolent Planets
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Judge hopefully when Jupiter and Venus are the most powerful planets in the figure, and contrariwise when the malefics are the strongest.
prerequisites: Compare the strengths of benefics versus infortunes in the figure.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Comparative condition, not merely presence of either class.
No numerical weights or calibrated outcome probabilities supplied.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The application of the Lord of the fourth
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Fourth-house ruler applying to conjunction of eighth-house ruler is said to prolong illness; if fourth ruler is an infortune, death is also asserted; if benevolent, the opposite is expected.
prerequisites: Fourth ruler applying to CONJUNCTION of eighth ruler.
Fortune/infortune nature of fourth ruler distinguishes fatal versus contrary claim.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Source gives no orb or precise timing.
Keep duration testimony distinct from death modifier.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: A Retrograde Planet Significator of the Disease
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Retrograde disease significator is associated with continuing illness, bodily consumption, worsening again and relapse.
prerequisites: The disease significator (not any arbitrary planet) is retrograde.
exceptions_and_modifiers: No degree of retrogradation or time threshold given.
The attributed symptoms are historical doctrine, not diagnosis.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Significator being stationary
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A stationary significator is linked to urge to vomit and variable illness, while combustion by the Sun is added for a mostly-fatal prognosis.
prerequisites: Significator stationary.
Combustion by Sun is an extra condition for the stated mostly-fatal prognosis.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Source explains station as time to work harm because not moving; historical rationale not astronomy-to-medical validation.
Distinguish varied disease from death.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: A Significator in his Fall or Detriment
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A significator in fall or detriment is said to show danger, distress and fear or distrust in the sick person.
prerequisites: Relevant significator in its astrological fall OR detriment.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Reported fear is not reliable evidence of an actual person's psychology.
No independent illness chart or case.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The ascendant and the Moone being afflicted
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Afflicted ascendant and Moon with the lord of one and dispositor of the other not likewise afflicted are said to show disease of the body rather than spirits.
prerequisites: Ascendant AND Moon afflicted.
Lord of one and dispositor of other not likewise afflicted.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Keep the original asymmetry and pronoun referents unformalized; the text does not identify a single preferred mapping of the two rulers.
Body/spirits distinction is historical medical psychology, not modern differential diagnosis.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: But the ascendant and Moone free from misfortune
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Unafflicted ascendant and Moon with unfortunate rulers are said to place illness in spirits rather than body; if both are afflicted, both body and mind are tormented; a malefic aspect to ascendant but not Moon indicates 'Animals' rather than body, with a converse.
prerequisites: Variant A: ascendant AND Moon free from misfortune, their lords unfortunate.
Variant B: both afflicted.
Variant C: malefic planet regards ascendant but not Moon; contrary case reserved.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Do not merge the three alternative configurations.
Keep the printed Animals/spirits terminology; no psychiatric diagnosis or modern anatomical replacement.
The scope of 'their Lords' and 'both' is not fully resolved.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Lord of the sixt in the ascendant
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Sixth-house ruler in ascendant, ninth, eleventh or tenth allegedly makes illness manifest; in seventh, fourth, twelfth or eighth it is hidden or unknown.
prerequisites: Place ruler of sixth in one of the named house sets.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Exact enumerated houses matter; do not replace with only angular/succedent groups.
Unlisted house positions have no explicit classification in this sentence.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: Moveable Signes easily cause the Disease to vary
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Movable signs make disease variable; fixed signs long and difficult to remove; common signs indicate return, movement between body parts or variation in how well the patient feels over time.
prerequisites: Sign quality assessed for course of disease.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The clause begins at PDF318 and continues on PDF319.
Related to but not independent of fourth-house sign-quality claim #4.
No calibrated chronicity estimate.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: In the beginning of Diseases
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: At the beginning of illness examine lunar malposition/affliction together with the favourable or unfavourable state of the ascendant ruler, then judge the combined testimony.
prerequisites: Illness beginning.
Moon and ascendant ruler both assessed.
exceptions_and_modifiers: This is a combination procedure, not an independently successful clinical predictor.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If the Nativity of the sick may be obtained
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: If the patient's natal chart is known, compare the Moon at initial decumbiture or question to where a natal infortune was, or to its square/opposition, to allege slower or more difficult cure.
prerequisites: An actual natal chart is obtainable.
Current lunar place overlays natal infortune's original position or named hard aspect.
Time of illness onset OR question as specified.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Do not synthesize the natal chart from unverified personal data.
Requires cross-chart comparison; no default exact orb.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If in the beginning of a sicknesse
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Illness Moon in natal sixth, fourth, seventh, eighth or twelfth together with an infortune at both times is said to signify death, unless a benefic casts favourable rays at one of those times.
prerequisites: Moon at start of illness in one of five listed natal houses.
An infortune occurs at both the natal AND sickness times.
No rescuing benefic beam at either time for adverse clause.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Benefic exception is explicitly stated; no unconditional natal-house death rule.
The grammatical referent of 'both times' is source-local and remains qualified.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: When the ascendant of the sicknesse is opposite
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Onset ascendant opposing the natal ascendant and falling among specified natal houses, with the revolution ascendant 'not the same', is associated with scarcely any recovery.
prerequisites: Onset ascendant opposite natal ascendant.
Onset ascendant corresponds to fourth, sixth, eighth, twelfth OR seventh in stated comparison.
Ascendant of Revolution not same, as printed.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Source involves natal, illness and Revolution frames and leaves the identity of 'same' elliptical.
Do not compute or substitute annual solar return from this sentence alone.
Strong prognosis is unverified historical assertion.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: When the Lord of the second doth infortunate
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Second-house ruler afflicting the ascendant ruler is said to make cure expensive; if the sick person dies, large expenditures are described as ineffective.
prerequisites: Second ruler afflicts ascendant ruler.
If death actually occurs, cost-wasted assertion is an additional branch.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Cost and death are separate outcome dimensions.
No price or quantified treatment cost.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Sun in the ascendant brings usually health
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Sun in ascendant is said usually to bring health immediately; Sun in sixth produces an immediate change; eighth ruler combust is associated with recovery rather than death 'at that time'.
prerequisites: Three alternative conditions: Sun in ascendant, Sun in sixth, OR eighth ruler combust.
exceptions_and_modifiers: 'Usually' and 'at that time' qualify timing; do not claim lifelong recovery.
A disease change in sixth is not automatically a cure.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Sun is the candle or light of Heaven
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: The Sun is poetically described as the illuminating spirit beautifying the signs it occupies and destroying nature's enemies.
prerequisites: Author's general rationale following a Sun-based prognosis.
exceptions_and_modifiers: This is explanatory rhetoric, not a separately predictive or case-based clinical rule.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: Fear not the death of thy Patient
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: A favourable Jupiter aspect to Sun is said to remove fear of death even though the ascendant ruler applies to the eighth ruler.
prerequisites: Jupiter in a good aspect to Sun.
Ascendant ruler applying to eighth ruler is an overridden adverse testimony.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Benefic override appears explicitly; no unspecified Sun/Jupiter dignities or orbs.
Source certainty is unvalidated.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: When a sicknesse takes one first
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: If the Moon is separating from Sun's combustion as sickness first strikes, the illness is said to grow until Moon opposes Sun.
prerequisites: At FIRST sickness onset, Moon separating from combustion.
Monitor until Moon's opposition to Sun.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Do not replace the aspect event with an assumed fixed number of days.
Disease-increase assertion, not confirmed outcome.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Lord of the ascendant being unfortunate in the eighth
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Unfortunate ascendant ruler in eighth is interpreted as patient's careless or bad management aggravating illness and delaying cure.
prerequisites: Ascendant ruler unfortunate IN the eighth.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The implied patient-blame or motive is not evidence of actual behaviour.
Distinguish the source claim from medically supported causal responsibility.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Significator of the sick Occidentally
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: An occidental sick-person significator is assigned chronic illness, an oriental one new illness; the Moon's separation and application are said to show disease decrease or increase.
prerequisites: Assess orientation of the actual sick-person significator.
Consider lunar separation and application.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Not all occidental charts are clinically chronic; source gives no precision/caseload.
Do not conflate oriental/orientated status with other uses of angular speed.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: If Saturn be author of the Disease
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Saturn as author of the illness is assigned cold; Mars or Sun assign heat and dryness; analogous planetary nature is invoked for the remaining planets.
prerequisites: Source first assigns an authoring planet of illness; interpret its attributed nature.
exceptions_and_modifiers: Printed aphorism spans PDF319–320.
No exhaustive correspondences for all remaining planets are supplied here.
Historical humoral attribution, not medical mechanism.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated

source_locator.passage_anchor: The Moone is more afflicted of Mars
source_locator.anchor_type: normalized locating phrase, not declared diplomatic quotation

rules.source_statement: Moon's increased light is said to make it more afflicted by Mars, its waning phase more oppressed by Saturn; Mars is said to do more harm when in masculine signs, oriental and above the Earth, with the contrary judgment for Saturn.
prerequisites: Waxing versus waning Moon treated separately.
Mars condition: masculine signs AND oriental AND above Earth in printed emphasis.
exceptions_and_modifiers: The Saturn converse is not a fully enumerated complementary Boolean rule in the source.
Avoid conflating waxing with speed or motion.
This is the last physician aphorism before Chapter XLV, which has a separate dated worked chart.
rules.source_attribution: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), printed chapter XLIV numbered physician aphorism; independent antecedent source not collated
